caption:
No Indian mother has ever thrown away a good box. It gets emptied and filled with buttons for twenty years.

Ours is blush, with a drawer and a little pull tab, and every piece arrives in one, in 3 to 5 working days.

Somewhere in 2040 it will be holding safety pins. That is the highest compliment we know.

Today's mangal: Urdu, منگل.

[ the naira box · blush, with a drawer · keep it ]
first_comment: What is in your mother's best box right now? Free insured shipping. Cash on delivery available. #NairaFlore #NairaPetite #Unboxing #JewelleryGift #DemiFineJewellery
alt_text: Short video on a bottle-green wall. Cover: a steel shelf holds a drawn stack of saved boxes, a dark red saree box with a gold border, a sage watch box and a purple shoe box, with handwritten tape labels reading buttons, warranty cards and rakhi, 2014. On top sits a real blush Naira jewellery box with a tape label reading naira. keep. Text: House rule 09, the top shelf. The good box is never thrown away. In 2040 it will hold safety pins. Under the shelf, the Naira wordmark and the word Mangal, also written in Urdu, beside a small steel key. In the video the boxes are stacked on the shelf one by one and the Naira box is set down on top, two photographs show real Naira boxes, one being slid open in two hands and one resting with its drawer open, and the end card shows the closed box with the words: every piece arrives in it. Free insured shipping. Cash on delivery available. Delivery in 3 to 5 working days. Keep the box. We would.

A first pass that cloned the edge strip from 170 px up the edge left a bright blob and was discarded (_work/r3/heal_petal.v1.py). EYEBROW COPY (AD fix pass). The spec's eyebrow 'HOUSE RULE N° 09 · THE GOOD BOX' sat directly above 'THE GOOD BOX IS / NEVER THROWN AWAY.' and said the phrase twice in two lines; every other rule's eyebrow names a setting (KARWA CHAUTH, THE LOCKER, CIRCA 2006, CHILDREN). WEDDING SEASON is P12's and is not used.

PHOTOS NOT FULL-BLEED. The spec scales the 1200x1490 listing photos to cover 1080x1920 (1546x1920, 1.29x their native size), which would upscale them. They run instead as a full-width plate, y 245-1675 (1080x1430, the image at 0.96, 36 px cropped each side), on the bottle-green ground; the push-in 1.00 to 1.04 ends at 0.998 of native. The plate fills almost exactly the part of the screen the Reels UI leaves visible.

THE REAL BOX IS TURNED LEVEL. In its photograph (cutouts/naira-box/a-closed-trim.png) the box sits about 17 degrees clockwise, so at the spec's rotate(2deg) its front edge sloped 19 degrees on a flat stack and it balanced on one corner. It is turned back 16.8 degrees (measured on the matte's front and back edges) so the front edge and the printed NAIRA run level and it reads front-on like the drawn boxes, plus B4's own -1.5 degrees: rotate(-18.3deg) on the cover, rotate(-16.8deg) on the end card. The petal stays as photographed.

REAL BOX SIZE. Because the turned box fills less of its image, it is displayed at 0.55 of native on the cover (image 425x417, the box itself about 345 px wide, the spec's 340) and 0.76 on the end card (image 587x576, box about 470 px wide, the spec's 460). Both are under native size. Its bottom edge sits flush on B4's top-front edge, like every box below it, so the satin pull tab drapes over B4's lid.

STACK CENTRED AND RAISED. The stack moves 50 px right (B1 x 250-810, plus its side face) so it stands on the seal's centre line x 540, and stack and shelf move 12 px up (shelf front y 1408-1430, brackets to 1460). At the spec's y the seal's chaabi ring touched the plank's underside and read as hung on it; it now clears it by 12 px.

BOX DRAWING. Each saved box gets a right side face (18 px, the box colour with 22% ink) as well as the spec's top face, so the oblique reads as a solid box: three fills and one 3.5 px #1F2E25 ink line per box. Small identity details in the same ink: the shoe box (B4) has a lid 6 px wider each side over its base, the watch box (B3) a hinge seam. The shelf has a 24 px top face in rim steel #E6E9E8 (the steel shorthand: #D9DDDC front, #A9B1B0 shade band). Brackets are 34x30 (spec 'to y 1466').

SUPERSEDED (grid pass r2: B2, the mithai box, is deleted): MITHAI BOX WINDOW (AD fix pass). The spec's window (x 430-550, y 1236-1294 at 40% cream, here x 480-600, y 1224-1282) in a full 3.5 px outline read at 391 px as a blank fifth tape label beside 'bindis'. Its outline is 2 px and one acetate glint, a 3 px #FBF3EC line at 70% with round caps, runs diagonally across its top-left corner from (522,1229) to (486,1265), about a third of the way across, so it reads as a window. Still three fills plus one ink line.
B4 ROTATION PIVOT. B4 turns -1.5 degrees about B3's top-left corner, so its lifted right end stays inside B3's 18 px top face instead of sinking into B3's front.

TIMING. The spec ended the shelf beat at 2.5 s, 0.35 s after 'naira. keep.' lands, which is too short to read the punchline (house rule: words hold 1.2 s or more). The shelf beat is held to 3.6 s ('naira. keep.' complete at 2.42 s). AD fix pass 2 retimed everything after it so that every change of scene is a dip through the bare bottle green: shelf layer out 3.60-3.80 (ease-in), photo 1 in 3.80-4.10 (ease-out) with its push-in from 3.80, a straight CUT to photo 2 at 5.10 (frame 153), photo 2 out 6.60-6.90 (ease-in), end-card box in 6.90-7.50, 'EVERY PIECE / ARRIVES IN IT.' types up at 7.45 s (0.15 s stagger), service lines rise at 7.95 s (0.12 s stagger), 'keep the box. we would.' fades in 8.45-9.05 s, held to 11.55 s (2.5 s). Without the customer photo the two photos run 1.3 s and 1.8 s (spec 1.5 s each): the AD set the cut at 5.10.

LOOP: A TWO-STEP DISSOLVE, NOT A CROSSFADE (AD fix passes 1 and 2). The single 0.55 s crossfade laid the end-card box under the cover headline and the end-card type over the shelf. Now the end card's box, headline, service lines and aside fade out 11.55-11.80 s on its own green (opacity 1 to 0, --ease-in); at 11.80 the end card goes and the frame-0 eyebrow, headline, turn and shelf fade in 11.80-12.00 s (--ease-out). The seal is identical in both states and never moves. Last frame vs frame 0: mean pixel difference 0.26.

THE REAL BOX IS SET DOWN, NOT DROPPED (AD fix pass). The spec drops it from -220 px; at that height it faded in as a see-through grey-green slab behind the headline and the turn. It is placed from -50 px over 0.6 s from 1.50 s, lands at 1.91 s (the fifth tap) and makes the reel's one 6 px settle. Its top ink measures y 653 on its first frame (1.533 s), 23 px under the turn's descenders (ink to y 630), and never rises higher. The four drawn boxes keep the spec's -160 px drop on a decelerating curve with no overshoot; tape labels press on (scale 1.14 to 1, 0.3 s, no overshoot) 0.04 s after their box lands, not the cookbook's 'stamp' (which overshoots and fixes the angle at -3 degrees). Opacity (AD fix pass 2): each drawn box is opaque at 12% of its fall (was 40%, the AD's fix), and the real box at 8% of its move (was 20%, beyond the AD's list: at 20% its first frame still showed it at about 30% as a grey-green slab), so all five are solid by their second frame.

END CARD CENTRED, SERVICE LINES LARGER (AD fix pass). The spec sets the end-card type at x 72 under a centred box; it is centred on x 540 (box, type and seal on one axis, as P08's end card). Velista 76 at 1000/1080 as specified. The three service lines are Jost 500 32 px at .16em (spec 26 px .2em, about 9 pt on a phone, the reel's smallest type for the beat that carries cash on delivery) on baselines 1166/1222/1278 (spec 1160/1208/1256); the widest spans x 189-896. 'keep the box. we would.' moves from baseline 1330 to 1356 (line box to y 1369, MANGAL from 1470). The box is centred at (540,630) instead of 640 so its shadow ends about 70 px above the headline.
WORDS AT x 72. Eyebrow and headline start at x 72 (system x 60) so in-video words stay inside x 72-1008, as P08 did.

SUPERSEDED (grid pass r1): SEAL. The system's P10 seal: no wordmark (the lid prints NAIRA); MANGAL cream with a blush back copy on a green keyline (system deviation 10). منگل (AD fix pass): front in date gold #E7C27A (was blush on a cream keyline, about 1.2:1), back copy blush +4/+4, green keyline (system deviations 9 and 11), at the spec's 34 px (was 30) on reel baseline 1606 (was 1601; spec 1588, where the gaf ran into MANGAL's foot). Made in _system/system.css so P6's Gujarati takes the same gold.

END CARD: A DIP THROUGH GREEN, NOT A WIPE (AD fix pass 2, the AD's own named alternative). The spec's wipe-up at .6s --ease-inout whipped (up to 290 px a frame) and sliced the box into view. The AD's primary fix, wipe-up .9s cubic-bezier(.37,0,.63,1) from 6.3 s, cannot meet its own acceptance: the clip travels 1,920 px, so sine in-out peaks at 1.587 x 1,920 / 27 = 113 px a frame (the 75-80 px estimate holds only for the 1,430 px photo plate). Confining the wipe to the plate still peaks at 83 px in 0.9 s, and photo pixels then stay on screen until 7.2 s, which pushes the box and the type later and cuts the end card's hold under 2.5 s. So the photo plate fades out 6.60-6.90 s (--ease-in) onto bare green, the box scales in 6.90-7.50 s (scale-in .6s --ease-out, drift from 7.50 s) with the end card's seal fading in beside it (.6s --ease-out), and the type follows at the AD's times. There is no wipe edge, and no frame holds a photo pixel once the box is visible.

RENDER GUARD. reel.html freezes every animation at t = 0 with a three-line inline script before the first paint, so the renderer only ever seeks forward. One render in this pass showed the mithai box resting on the empty shelf, and a faint 'buttons' tape, from frame 0 to frame 10: the renderer seeks back from the page's running clock and Chromium sometimes kept a stale paint for an element seeked back into its delay. tools/reel.cjs is shared and is not changed.
